title: Parser rejects `FN:` records with negative line numbers, then deadlocks when panics happen in worker threads
body:
## Summary

`grcov`'s lcov parser rejects `FN:<line>,<name>` records where `<line>` is negative (e.g. `FN:-1,...`) and **discards the entire input file's coverage data** as a result. When many worker threads panic in parallel during multi-file processing, the main thread also `futex_wait`s indefinitely on results the panicked workers never produce, and `grcov` hangs at ~0 % CPU with no exit and no useful output.

JaCoCo emits `FN:-1,...` for synthetic/generated methods that lack a source line — Scala auto-generated `.curried` / `.tupled` on case classes, macro-expanded methods, etc. — so any medium-sized Scala/JVM project routes through this bug the first time `grcov` merges its coverage output.

## Environment

- `grcov 0.10.7`, `grcov-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl` from the GitHub release.
- Input: lcov `.info` files emitted by Bazel `bazel coverage --combined_report=lcov` for a Scala/JVM codebase (JaCoCo → lcov converter).

## Minimal reproducer — parse fault / data loss

Save as `in/test.info`:

```
TN:
SF:foo.scala
FN:-1,curried
FNDA:0,curried
FNF:1
FNH:0
DA:1,0
LF:1
LH:0
end_of_record
```

Run:

```
grcov in -t lcov -o out.info
```

### Actual output

`grcov` stderr:

```
[ERROR] Error parsing file /path/to/in: Invalid record: 'FN at line 3'
```

`out.info` contains only `TN:` — the file's entire coverage data is silently discarded.

### Expected

Either accept negative line numbers (parse as `i32` / treat as "synthetic, no source location"), or skip only the malformed record and preserve the rest of the file's coverage.

## Empirical narrowing

Same input with only the FN's line number changed:

| `FN:` value | Result |
|---|---|
| `FN:-1,curried`     | FAIL — whole file dropped |
| `FN:-999,curried`   | FAIL — same |
| `FN:-1,name (I)Z`   | FAIL — same (space in name is irrelevant) |
| `FN:0,curried`      | OK  |
| `FN:1,curried`      | OK  |
| `FN:1,name (I)Z`    | OK — space in JVM signature is fine |
| `FN:,curried`       | FAIL (expected — empty line number) |

`FN:0` succeeds but `FN:-1` fails, which strongly suggests the parser reads the line-number field as an unsigned integer and any leading `-` fails the parse. Fix likely at `src/parser.rs:194` (the site named by the accompanying panic — see below).

## Deadlock repro (needs real-scale input)

At real-world scale — hundreds of `.info` files, several GB total, real JVM signatures — the parse fault escalates to a **deadlock**: some worker threads emit a panic

```
[ERROR] A panic occurred at src/parser.rs:194: called `Option::unwrap()` on a `None` value
```

while others emit the softer

```
[ERROR] Error parsing file <dir>: Invalid record: 'FN at line N'
```

The main thread then `futex_wait`s forever on channels the panicked workers never send to. Observed reliably with 658 files / ~1.6 GB from Bazel coverage of ~300 Scala tests; process sits at ~0 % CPU indefinitely (killed manually after 10 min):

```
$ ps -p <pid> -o pcpu,etime,stat
%CPU     ELAPSED  STAT
 0.0    00:35     Sl

$ for t in $(ls /proc/<pid>/task/); do
    echo "  tid=$t state=$(awk '/^State/{print $2}' /proc/<pid>/task/$t/status) wchan=$(cat /proc/<pid>/task/$t/wchan)"
  done
  tid=<main>   state=S wchan=futex_do_wait
  tid=<worker> state=S wchan=futex_do_wait
```

### Repro script

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Reproduce with real Bazel + JaCoCo coverage output.
# 1. Clone a small-to-medium Scala repo that uses rules_scala (any case-class-heavy Scala repo works)
# 2. Add a `coverage`-tagged test to enough targets that `bazel coverage //...` runs 300+ tests.
# 3. Wire grcov as the coverage_report_generator:
#      # in .bazelrc
#      coverage --coverage_report_generator=//tools:grcov_report_generator
#    where //tools:grcov_report_generator is an sh_binary wrapping grcov that reads
#    --reports_file (a text file listing lcov .dat paths) and calls
#    `grcov <staging-dir-symlinked-from-reports-file> -t lcov -o <output>`.
# 4. Run `bazel coverage //...` and watch the "Coverage report generation" step.
#    It will hang past the point where the Java LcovMerger would finish.

# Alternative: if you already have a Bazel + Scala coverage run's outputs on disk,
# stage them into one directory and hand that to grcov directly:
STAGING=$(mktemp -d)
find bazel-out -path '*/testlogs/*/coverage.dat' -o -name 'baseline_coverage.dat' \
  | awk 'BEGIN{i=0} {printf "%s %s\n", $0, i++}' \
  | while read src idx; do ln -sf "$(readlink -f "$src")" "$STAGING/$idx.dat"; done

timeout 30 grcov "$STAGING" -t lcov -o /tmp/out.info
echo "exit=$?"     # 124 (SIGTERM from timeout) confirms the hang
wc -c /tmp/out.info  # near-zero — no useful merged output produced
```

### Pure-synthetic attempt (does NOT reproduce the deadlock — only the parse fault)

I could not shrink the deadlock to a fully self-contained script — synthetic input with hundreds of files each containing `FN:-1` records exits cleanly with "Invalid record" logs, no panic and no hang. The panic path appears to need the combination of BRDA branch records + realistic JVM signature strings + interleaved good/bad FN records + real per-file scale (multi-MB per file, ~1.6 GB aggregate) that JaCoCo output produces.

## Possible fix

1. **Parser**: at `src/parser.rs:194`, accept negative integers for the FN line number (parse as `i32`, or treat any non-parseable line number as "unknown" and store as `None`/`0`). Skip only the malformed record if a strict parse is preferred — do not drop the whole file.
2. **Defence-in-depth for worker panics**: wrap the per-file worker in `catch_unwind` (or send an explicit error variant over the results channel on panic) so a panicked worker does not leave the main thread `futex_wait`ing forever. This is independent of the parser fix and would eliminate the observed hang even if some future malformed input triggers a similar unwrap.

## Real-world context

Surfaced wiring `grcov` as Bazel's `--coverage_report_generator` for a ~300-test Scala repo using rules_scala + JaCoCo. Every Scala target with an auto-generated `.curried` / `.tupled` (i.e. essentially every `case class`) contributes at least one `FN:-1,...` record, so once one Scala coverage target exists in a repo of this scale, `grcov` hangs on every subsequent coverage merge.

title: [Feature request] gcov format version 2 support
body:
GCC 14 bumped its `gcov` intermediate JSON schema to `"format_version": "2"`. And using `grcov` together with it generates this error:

```
[ERROR] Format version 2 is not expected, please file a bug on https://github.com/mozilla/grcov
```

This is triggered in [`src/parser.rs`](https://github.com/mozilla/grcov/blob/master/src/parser.rs):

```rust
if gcov.format_version != "1" {
    error!(
        "Format version {} is not expected, please file a bug on https://github.com/mozilla/grcov",
        gcov.format_version
    );
}
```

Currently `grcov` still generates coverage report which seems to be correct despite of this error message. But I am not very sure whether the best fix is to remove this check directly.

Reproduction (has a dockerfile so we have gcc14 environment):

[grcov-gcc14-repro.tar.gz](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29344934/grcov-gcc14-repro.tar.gz)

title: `grcov` can panic on several malformed coverage inputs instead of reporting parse/output errors
LCOV parser breaks on DA lines with optional checksum field
body:
The LCOV format allows an optional checksum field on DA lines: `DA:line_number,execution_count[,checksum]`

grcov's byte-level LCOV parser does not consume the optional checksum field after reading the execution count. Depending on what character the checksum starts with, this causes different issues.


1. checksum starts with `e` (interpreted as `end_of_record`):
```
SF:test.py
DA:1,0,e3ZBlmsTAEA3QwKvJLg9CA
LH:0
LF:1
end_of_record
A panic occurred at src/parser.rs:194: called `Option::unwrap()` on a `None` value
```

2. checksum starts with a valid key prefix like `FN`, `DA`, `FNDA`:
```
SF:test.py
DA:1,0,FNsomechecksum
LH:0
LF:1
end_of_record
Error parsing file: Invalid record: 'FN at line 3'
```

3. checksum starts with `SF` or `BRDA`:
```
SF:test.py
DA:1,0,SFsomechecksum
LH:0
LF:1
end_of_record
No error, but the checksum is interpreted as a new source file record, silently corrupting the output.
```

I have tried tackling the issue here https://github.com/mozilla/grcov/pull/1500 before realising it is more widespread, and not isolated to just checksums starting with `e`.

title: How to merge coverage data
body:
Hi! I might be missing something totally obvious, but I'm wondering how to merge (combine) C++ coverage from GCC? 

gcovr has something like this: https://gcovr.com/en/stable/output/json.html#json-format-merging

Is there similar functionality available in grcov?

My use case isn't that special: I have many parallel runs of my software (on different machines), and I want to collect coverage for all of them and present them as a unified HTML report.

title: Symbolic 12.16 bumps MSRV from 1.73 to 1.82
body:
Just a heads up, we're bumping the msrv in symbolic-demangle and symbolic-common from 1.73 to 1.82, as the rest of symbolic already implicitly (through dependencies) requires 1.82, so we cannot realistically guarantee the MSRV.

You do have users using grcov with older Rust version, e.g. [here 1.75](https://github.com/mozilla/grcov/issues/1284). In the readme 1.52 is mentioned as MSRV.

To stay MSRV compatible you'd have to stay with the 12.15 release, which works for 1.73.
